DATA SHEET FOR BUCKET WHEEL RECLAIMER 

(RAIL MOUNTED) 

PART 2 INFORMATION TO BE SUPPLIED BY THE PURCHASER 



ICS 53.020.99

BUREAU OF INDIAN STANDARDS 

MANAK BHAVAN, 9 BAHADUR SHAH ZAFAR MARG 
NEW DELHI 110002 

February 2000 Price Group 3 



Bulk Handling Systems and Equipment Sectional Committee, ME 07 



FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Bulk 
Handling Systems and Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering 
Division Council. 

This standard is expected to provide a uniform practice for manufacturers and users for laying down data 
for selection of rail mounted bucket wheel reclaimers. 



IS 12663 (Part 2) : 2000 

Indian Standard 

BULK HANDLING EQUIPMENT — RECLAIMER — 
DATA SHEET FOR BUCKET WHEEL RECLAIMER 

(RAIL MOUNTED) 

PART 2 INFORMATION TO BE SUPPLIED BY THE PURCHASER 



1 SCOPE 

This standard lays down the data required for selection of rail mounted bucket wheel reclaimers.

2.6 Travel Carriage Details 

a) Type of travel carriage drive: 

(Single speed/Variable speed/Stepped speed) 

b) Type of wheel — Single flanged/Double flanged 

c) Type of wheel bearing required

2.7 Method of Ventilation/Air-Conditioning of Operator's Cabin — Pressurized/AC/Fan 

2.8 Additional Features Required 

a) The equipment shall have rail clam.ping arrangements alongwith interlocking or travel drive motors 
to be used during operation/standstill condition. 

b) The equipment shall have flood lighting arrangements on both sides. 

c) Type of controls for reclaiming operation — Manual/Automatic. 

d) Type of supporting — Three leg/Four leg support. 

e) Lubrication 

i) Type of lubrication desired — Centralized/Groupwise. 
ii) All lubrication points to be easily accessible. 

iii) Groupwise lubrication clubbing different zones of lubrication points under different groups to 

be specified 

iv) All the angular movement points (hinge point) may be provided with maintenance free bearing 
requiring no periodic lubrication during entire life span. 

f) The provision of end buffers at both ends of machine travel — Yes/No 

g) Safety device for excessive reeling of cable reeling drum to prevent possible cable rupture to be 
provided — Yes/No 

h) Type of ventilation/air-conditioning for electric house and whether insulation required 

j) Flood light attachment at bucket wheel for proper visibility in and around reclaiming zone 
(Lights shall be suitable for the dust penetration). 

k) W^hether programmable logic control required — Yes/No 

m) Whether buckets/cutting tips replaceable — Yes/No

i) Whether attached wheel jacks required — Yes/No 

ii) Whether anti-collision device required — Yes/No 

iii) Whether the reclaimer is to operate in conjunction with a separate stacker mounted on the same 
yard conveyor — Yes/No

of the track on either side of the track (m)

u) Shape of stockpile — Trapezoidal/Triangular 

v) Maximum permissible wheel load 

w) Angle of slew 



x) Whether impact cradle required as part of reclaimer — Yes/No 



Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of stardardization, marking and quality certification of goods and 
attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form 
without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of 
implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. 
Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publication), BIS 

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue 
of 'BIS Handbook' and 'Standards: Monthly Additions'. 

This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc: No. MED 7 (0461).
